lines: Prepare a paper trade before acting.
Open Trade, and check the instrument you are viewing.
Choose Buy or Sell deliberately. We will use Buy.
Check the order type. This example uses Market.
Set the lot size. This is an illustrative practice account.
Enable Stop Loss, then enter your exercise's stop level.
Enable Take Profit, then enter your exercise's target.
Pause to review the estimated loss and margin.
Reduce the lot size, and check how the estimate changes.
Recheck direction, size, stop and target. These are estimates.
Stop here with the prepared ticket. No order was submitted.
A clear chart starts with one useful observation.
First, check the market you are viewing.
Choose one timeframe before adding any drawings.
Look for a price area you want to observe.
Select H-Line in the drawing toolbar.
Click once on the chart to mark that level.
Pause and check where your line landed.
Return to Cursor when you finish drawing.
A marked level does not guarantee a price reaction.
Practise marking one level, then explain why you chose it.
Review one detected pattern in its chart context.
First, check the market and the selected timeframe.
Open Scanner beneath the chart.
Choose one result and read the pattern name.
Check whether its direction is bullish, bearish, or neutral.
Its score is a review cue, not a win probability.
Turn on Patterns to see the available chart overlay.
Compare the overlay with the candles you are viewing.
Look for evidence that could contradict the idea.
If the setup is unclear, wait and ask your instructor.
Turn one paper result into a useful learning reflection.
After a practice close, open Journal beneath the chart.
Start with the newest close at the top.
Read the trade direction and instrument together.
Check the volume that was closed.
Then read the paper result. Profit alone proves little.
A partial close can create another row for one position.
For a learning record, use your Academy lesson's practice notes.
Write one thing you would review next time.
Save your reflection, and ask a lesson question if needed.
Learn two useful shortcuts for your desktop keyboard.
First, click outside any text input.
Press question mark to open Keyboard Shortcuts.
Start with A for Aria, and P for Portfolio.
Close help with Escape, then press A.
Pause, then press P to open Portfolio.
On a phone, use the visible tabs instead.
Practise these two shortcuts at your own pace.
Understand why Aria says to wait.
Begin by checking the market and timeframe.
Open Aria to inspect its checks.
Read the market conditions before looking at the score.
A passed gate means one rule matched.
Now read a condition that failed.
Read the verdict, including any restriction.
Ask what evidence would invalidate this idea.
In this example, we wait and leave the ticket alone.
Bring your reasoning to the lesson. Matching checks cannot guarantee results.
Understand Oracle's percentage before using it.
Open Oracle for the chart you are reviewing.
In this example, eight of the nine checks pass.
Eight divided by nine rounds to eighty-nine percent.
This is confluence: a count of conditions that agree.
It is not the probability that a trade will win.
Oracle and Aria use the same checks, so they are not independent confirmations.
In another example, only six of nine checks agree.
Read the reasons. Aria says waiting, so leave Apply unused.
Tools help you prepare. Review the evidence, and decide with care.
